answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that decays along a spiral of diminishing returns: the first identity is cheap, but every additional identity costs exponentially more, so a bot farm faces a canyon of rising expense while honest users pay almost nothing. New identities start with zero trust and must earn attestation from established peers over time; a zephyr of fresh accounts cannot flood the market because unvouched work earns no payout until the stake matures and peers confirm real output.
